notable_absence.finding: The Server 8.0 page has *lost* three of the four availability badges its Capella twin carries. Capella heads EVALUATE() with 'Couchbase Server 8.0', HASHBYTES() with 'Couchbase Server 8.0', and FINDERR() with 'Couchbase Server 7.6.5'; the Server 8.0 page carries none of those three, retaining the badge only on EXTRACTDDL(). Since all four functions are on both pages, three availableSince facts are recoverable *only* from the Capella record. The retention of EXTRACTDDL's badge alongside the removal of EVALUATE's and HASHBYTES's - all three of which are 8.0 features - looks like an editing oversight rather than a policy, because the treatment is inconsistent within a single page.

cross_component_finding: Two things worth reconciliation's attention. (1) The finderr CLI cross-reference and the FINDERR() SQL++ function are the same diagnostic capability exposed through two surfaces, and the Server page links them explicitly while the Capella page cannot (no CLI surface exists there); this is one of the cleaner examples in the batch of a link that is absent for genuine product-shape reasons rather than editorial ones. (2) A naming inconsistency this page exposes: it calls query_system_catalog a *role* ('you must have the `query_system_catalog` role'), whereas earlier extraction records filed the same string under the privilege: namespace (privilege:query-system-catalog, minted from the AWR and system-catalog pages). Couchbase's own RBAC reference treats query_system_catalog as a role that grants a privilege of the same name, so both readings are defensible - but the ontology cannot hold it in both namespaces. I have reused the existing privilege: id as the object while using requiresRole as the predicate, which is internally inconsistent and deliberately so, to make the collision visible rather than silently pick a side.
cross_product_finding: The Capella twin is again the richer source of version facts (same pattern as searchfun.md and stringfun.md in this batch): Capella badges EVALUATE, EXTRACTDDL and HASHBYTES as 'Couchbase Server 8.0' and FINDERR as 'Couchbase Server 7.6.5'; Server 8.0 keeps only the EXTRACTDDL badge. Two further divergences: (a) the privilege statement is expressed in entirely different access models - Server says 'you must have the `query_system_catalog` role', Capella says 'your client must have Read access if using basic access credentials, or Query Catalog privilege if using advanced access credentials'; these are NOT merged, and the correspondence (Server role query_system_catalog <-> Capella privilege:capella-advanced-access-query-catalog) is recorded here as a finding only. (b) The CURRENT_USERS() example output differs by product in a way that reveals the identity model: Server returns 'builtin:Administrator', Capella returns 'local:<redacted-UUID>'. That is a real, documented behavioural difference in a function's return value across products, and there is currently no predicate for 'returns different values on different deployments' - deployment:capella exists as a concept, so behavesDifferentlyUnder deployment:capella would be expressible, but I have not asserted it because neither page says the other product behaves differently; the difference is only visible by comparing the two.
version_finding: Harvest from this page: EXTRACTDDL availableSince version:server-8-0; two of its flag values (function, prepared) availableSince version:server-8-0-1; the 15-XATTR-per-query limit at version:server-8-0; and the META()+SEARCH() XATTRs combination at version:server-7-6-2. The 8.0.1 case is the most interesting for vocabulary design and is new in this wave: a page published as 'server/current' at version 8.0 gates two option values on 8.0.1, a release *later* than the page's own version. Any model that assumes 'the page's version is the floor for everything it documents' breaks here, and a reader on 8.0.0 is being shown two flag values they cannot use. Also note the version-badge convention itself is fragile as evidence: the badge is a bare line of text ('Couchbase Server 8.0') under a heading, with no marker distinguishing it from body prose, and inline badges are concatenated into list items and table cells ('CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION Couchbase Server 8.0.1 "function" 32'), which is why the same fact appears twice on this page in two different renderings. Finally, a documentation defect for the record: DS_VERSION()'s worked example on the Couchbase Server 8.0 page returns '7.6.0-1886-enterprise' - a stale example output two minor versions behind the page it appears on, on the one function whose entire job is to report the version.
